title: Maximal Rectangle
description:
Given a rows x cols binary matrix filled with '0's and '1's, find the largest rectangle containing only '1's and return its area.

The rectangle must be axis-aligned and consist entirely of '1' cells. If the matrix has no '1' cells, the area is 0.

examples.explanation: The maximal rectangle of 1's has area 6, spanning the bottom-middle block of the matrix.
There are no 1 cells, so the largest rectangle has area 0.
A single 1 cell forms a rectangle of area 1.

approach: Process the matrix row by row, maintaining a histogram where heights[c] is the number of consecutive '1' cells ending at the current row in column c; a '0' resets that column to 0. The largest all-ones rectangle whose bottom edge lies on the current row is exactly the largest rectangle in this histogram. Compute that with a monotonic increasing stack of (startIndex, height): when a shorter bar appears, pop taller bars and measure the area each spans, carrying the popped start index leftward. Appending a sentinel height of 0 flushes the stack at the end of each row. For R rows and C columns the work is O(R * C).
